subject: English
topic: Active and Passive Voice — Transformation across Tenses (W12 B1)

questions.stem: Change to passive voice: 'She writes a letter every day.'

options.option_text: A letter is written by her every day.
A letter was written by her every day.
A letter is being written by her every day.
A letter will be written by her every day.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Simple Present Active → Simple Present Passive: Object + is/are + V3 + by + Subject. 'She writes' → 'is written by her'. The time phrase 'every day' stays unchanged. Trap: 'was written' = Simple Past passive (wrong tense); 'is being written' = Present Continuous passive (wrong — original is habitual, not ongoing now).

questions.stem: Change to passive voice: 'He ate the food.'

options.option_text: The food is eaten by him.
The food was eaten by him.
The food has been eaten by him.
The food had been eaten by him.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Simple Past Active → Simple Past Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject. 'He ate' → 'was eaten by him'. Subject 'food' is singular → 'was'. Trap: 'is eaten' = Present tense (wrong — original is past tense 'ate'); 'has been eaten' = Present Perfect passive (past action but with present relevance — the original simply uses Simple Past); 'had been eaten' = Past Perfect passive (too far back — implies another past event happened after).

questions.stem: Change to passive voice: 'They will complete the project.'

options.option_text: The project is completed by them.
The project has been completed by them.
The project will be completed by them.
The project was completed by them.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Simple Future Active → Simple Future Passive: Object + will be + V3 + by + Subject. 'Will complete' → 'will be completed by them'. Trap: 'is completed' = Simple Present passive (wrong tense); 'has been completed' = Present Perfect passive (wrong — original uses future 'will'); 'was completed' = Simple Past passive (wrong tense).

questions.stem: Change to passive voice: 'The teacher has taught the students.'

options.option_text: The students are taught by the teacher.
The students were taught by the teacher.
The students have been taught by the teacher.
The students had been taught by the teacher.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Present Perfect Active → Present Perfect Passive: Object + has/have been + V3 + by + Subject. Subject is 'the students' (plural) → 'have been'. 'Has taught' → 'have been taught by the teacher'. Trap: 'are taught' = Simple Present passive (missing the 'have been' perfect aspect); 'had been taught' = Past Perfect passive (no past reference point was established — original is Present Perfect).

questions.stem: Change to passive voice: 'We are making a film.'

options.option_text: A film is made by us.
A film was being made by us.
A film has been made by us.
A film is being made by us.

questions.explanation: D is correct. Present Continuous Active → Present Continuous Passive: Object + is/are being + V3 + by + Subject. 'We are making' → 'is being made by us' (singular 'a film' → 'is being'). Key: the distinctive Continuous passive uses 'being'. Trap: 'is made' = Simple Present passive (drops the continuous aspect); 'was being made' = Past Continuous passive (wrong tense); 'has been made' = Present Perfect passive (wrong aspect).

questions.stem: Change to passive voice: 'She was writing a novel when the lights went out.'

options.option_text: A novel was written by her when the lights went out.
A novel was being written by her when the lights went out.
A novel had been written by her when the lights went out.
A novel is being written by her when the lights went out.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Past Continuous Active → Past Continuous Passive: Object + was/were being + V3 + by + Subject. 'Was writing' → 'was being written by her'. The time clause 'when the lights went out' remains unchanged. Trap: 'was written' = Simple Past passive (loses the ongoing/continuous aspect that was present in 'was writing'); 'had been written' = Past Perfect passive (implies completion before another past event — not what the original means).

questions.stem: Change to passive voice: 'They had finished the work before noon.'

options.option_text: The work was finished before noon.
The work has been finished before noon.
The work had been finished before noon by them.
The work will have been finished before noon by them.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Past Perfect Active → Past Perfect Passive: Object + had been + V3 + by + Subject. 'Had finished' → 'had been finished by them'. The time phrase 'before noon' remains. Trap: 'was finished' = Simple Past passive (drops the 'had been' perfect-before-past aspect); 'has been finished' = Present Perfect (wrong tense — original is Past Perfect).

questions.stem: Change to passive voice: 'Who broke the window?'

options.option_text: Who was the window broken by?
By whom was the window broken?
The window was broken by whom?
By whom the window was broken?

questions.explanation: B is correct. Interrogative Active with 'who' → Passive: 'By whom was the Object + V3?' The question word 'who' (subject in active) becomes 'by whom' (agent phrase in passive), and the verb inverts into question form: 'was...broken'. Trap: 'Who was the window broken by?' = ends with a preposition (incorrect formal style; also 'who' should become 'whom'); 'The window was broken by whom?' = statement word order (not a question); 'By whom the window was broken?' = subject-verb order wrong (no inversion).

questions.stem: Change to passive voice: 'People say that he is honest.'

options.option_text: He is said that he is honest.
It is said that he is honest by people.
It is said that he is honest.
He is said to have been honest.

questions.explanation: C is correct. The 'it-cleft' passive for reporting verbs: 'People say that...' → 'It is said that...'. The agent 'by people' is dropped as it is generic/obvious. An equivalent form: 'He is said to be honest.' (Using infinitive in second passive structure.) Trap: 'He is said that he is honest' = grammatically wrong (cannot have two subjects 'he' and 'he is honest' in this structure); 'It is said by people' = technically correct but the 'by people' is redundant and atypical for generic agents; 'He is said to have been honest' = wrong tense (implies past honesty, not present).

questions.stem: Identify the correct ACTIVE voice version of: 'I was asked to submit the report by the manager.'

options.option_text: The manager asked me to submit the report.
The manager was asking me to submit the report.
I asked the manager to submit the report.
The manager had been asking me to submit the report.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Passive: 'I was asked to submit the report by the manager.' → Active: Subject (manager) + V (asked) + Object (me) + infinitive (to submit the report). The passive uses Simple Past 'was asked' → active uses Simple Past 'asked'. The agent 'by the manager' becomes the active subject 'the manager'. Trap: 'was asking' = Past Continuous (wrong — 'was asked' is Simple Past passive); 'I asked the manager' = reverses subject and object (now I'm asking, not the manager); 'had been asking' = Past Perfect Continuous (wrong tense).
